name: Clínica Las Condes
lede: At a Santiago hospital, three restaurant terraces were too hot in summer and unusable in winter, with icy winds off the Andes. Thirty-two Tungsten Electric heaters, planned into new bioclimatic pergolas, keep them open all year for patients, visitors and staff.

hero.caption: Tungsten Smart-Heat® Electric – a product photograph, not this project. The case study carries no photographs of the terraces.

beats: Clínica Las Condes wanted comfortable outdoor areas for patients, visitors and staff. Its three restaurant terraces had only sunshades and lie open to cold winds from the Andes.
The architect asked for a powerful electric heating solution, so the new outdoor spaces could be used all year, within the hospital’s guidelines for renewable electricity.

Bromic’s Daniel Bruntsch recommended Tungsten Smart-Heat Electric and chose the 6000 W model with the client. Thirty-two heaters were planned into new louvred bioclimatic pergolas, directing radiant heat over the seating.
